newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO delays panel on US row with EU grain tariffs.
newsitem.headline: WTO delays panel on US row with EU grain tariffs.

text.p: The United States made a new bid for a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel to rule on its complaint against European Union grain tariffs, but the EU blocked it saying bilateral talks continued, trade sources said.
It was the second month in a row that Washington tried to formally bring the long-running dispute between the two powers to the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) for adjudication.

The United States argues that a new EU tariff system based on a reference price for wheat, rye, barley, corn, sorghum and rice, introduced in 1995, runs against agreements in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of global trade talks.

The EU said it was not willing to accept the U.S. request for establishment of a neutral WTO panel at this meeting as bilateral talks continued in Washington to find a solution. It would be appropriate to pursue the U.S. request only if and when consultations had definitively broken down, it added.
Washington first sought a WTO panel in October 1995, but the EU blocked the request in the DSB, saying talks continued.

U.S. sources have said that later that year, an agreement was reached and confirmed in an exchange of letters, and the request for a panel was withdrawn. But Washington argues Brussels has not implemented the accord.
